keywords: python loop loops for while range iterate iteration repeat print break continue
facts: A for loop runs its body once for each item in a sequence.
range(n) gives the numbers 0 up to n minus 1; range(start, stop, step) never includes stop.
The loop body is the indented block under the for line.
A while loop repeats as long as its condition is true.
break leaves a loop immediately; continue skips to the next pass.

scenes.heading: How does a Python loop work?
scenes.subtitle: Repeat an instruction for every value

narration.text: A loop repeats the same instruction for each value in a sequence.
The first line says: for each value i in range of three.
Range of three gives three values: zero, one and two.
The indented line is the body. It runs once for every value.
On the first pass, i is zero, so it prints zero.
Next, i becomes one, and it prints one.
Then i becomes two, and it prints two.
There are no values left, so the loop stops.

scenes.heading: Step 3: A loop with a condition

narration.text: We start a running total at zero.
The loop takes each number from the list in turn.
The if line keeps only odd numbers, where n mod two is one.
Seven and nine are odd, so the total becomes sixteen.

scenes.heading: Step 4: While loops and break

narration.text: A while loop repeats as long as its condition is true.
Each pass subtracts three: ten, seven, then four.
Break stops the loop at once, even though n is still above zero.
So the program prints four.

scenes.heading: Step 9: Common mistake: off by one

narration.text: Range of five starts at zero.
It gives zero, one, two, three and four.
That is five values, but the number five itself is never included.
